headline: Meta's Muse agent now shops and pays for users at Shopify stores and big retailers, while Amazon keeps it out.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: the checkout capability and retail partners date from September, and the 3 Oct CNBC piece is an explainer; the possible new detail of checkout fees could not be verified.
importance_line: Shoppers using Meta's Muse can let the agent buy for them at Shopify stores and soon at chains like Walmart and Best Buy, which changes how retailers and advertisers reach customers, but Amazon's block shows the biggest stores can still shut agents out and the reported checkout fees remain unconfirmed.
summary: AI News Desk, drawing on BigGo Finance and Fox News reporting, notes that Meta's Muse, the personal AI agent launched on 8 Sep 2026, can browse stores, compare prices and complete a purchase, pausing for the user's approval before money moves; Shopify made its Shop Pay wallet available inside Muse on 23 Sep 2026, Meta named Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Ulta and Wayfair as coming retail partners, and Stripe's Link wallet issues a one-time card number so neither the merchant nor the agent sees the real card. Amazon has blocked Muse from its site, citing rules that agents must identify themselves, so the first real test of agent shopping is whether retailers choose to open or close their doors.
notes: CNBC original blocked (403); facts from BigGo Finance (4 Oct) and Fox News (3 Oct). url is the CNBC article named in the pool; the text was read at https://finance.biggo.com/news/9d011a62-47fe-424e-8eb4-bdba605166d6. Checkout-fee detail in blocked outlets' headlines not included.
